subject: [Velox] Request funnel hang / p99 spikes — investigation & exec summary
messages:
From: Tom Redding <tom@velox.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Velox Platform Ops <ops@velox.ai>, Dina Lopez <dina@velox.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes + 429s in request funnel — urgent

Hannah,

We started seeing a series of p99 latency spikes last night (20:30-23:15 PDT) on our production calls routed through your hosted endpoint. Rough summary:
- ~15% of requests hit >2.5s p99 for inference (baseline was ~450ms)
- Elevated 429 error rate (~1.2% of requests) and a ~30% drop in sustained throughput for a 45-minute window
- Our internal traces show long queues waiting at the gateway before being accepted by your runtime; we attached a sample trace (velox_trace_0619.txt).

This is impacting our checkout flow (Velox Checkout) for a handful of high-value customers. We need an immediate timeline for mitigation and an explanation of root cause. Please loop in engineering and let us know whether this is an autoscaling/backpressure issue on your side (we didn't change traffic patterns).

Regards,
Tom Redding
Sr. SRE, Velox AI

Attachments: velox_trace_0619.txt
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Redding <tom@velox.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes + 429s in request funnel — urgent

Tom — thanks for the fast heads up and for the trace. I'm escalating this to our on-call infra and CS immediately. Quick notes from our side before our triage:
- We see a concurrent incident alert for a dedicated pool serving Velox that hit a concurrency cap between 20:28–21:12 PDT.
- We're opening an incident channel and pulling request logs and kernel metrics; attaching a high-level latency snapshot we generated from our tracing (redwood_latency_snapshot_20270619.pdf).

Immediate actions:
1) Marcus and infra will validate whether the concurrency cap, prefix cache eviction, or kernel scheduling caused head-of-line blocking.
2) Monica will coordinate a 30-min sync with your ops to review traces and routing.
3) I'll prepare an exec note for potential SLA credit/comp if this is on our side.

Can you confirm whether Velox had any burst traffic from 20:00–22:00 PDT (e.g., campaign or batch job)?

Hannah
Director, Customer Success (Redwood Inference)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_latency_snapshot_20270619.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes + 429s in request funnel — urgent

Hannah / team — preliminary findings from a quick dive into the telemetry:
- Concurrency cap: the dedicated pool for Velox briefly hit the configured concurrent-request ceiling (configured concurrency = 120) which caused the fronting router to return 429s when backlog exceeded the circuit thresholds.
- Backpressure & queueing: we observed long tail queues in the per-model request queue — starvation occurred because KV-cache refill (cold-start of several warm-up tokens after a small model switch earlier that day) caused CPU bursts on a subset of hosts, which delayed scheduler dispatch for ~30–45s windows.
- Autoscaler behavior: the autoscaler attempted to add capacity but was slow due to vCPU quota throttle in the customer's preferred cloud region; additional instances came up ~7 minutes after the initial cap was hit and after the worst of the spikes.

Short-term mitigations we recommend immediately:
A) Temporarily increase concurrency ceiling on Velox's dedicated pool from 120 -> 180 where host memory allows (risk: higher per-host memory usage).
B) Enable a targeted model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for non-paying background routes to reduce token compute per request.
C) Apply an emergency patch to the scheduler to prioritize inflight KV-cache warmups for pinned prefixes (will require a quick roll with a canary).

I've attached the autoscaler metrics (autoscaler_metrics_0619.csv). If leadership agrees, we can push A and B within a 30-minute maintenance window; C needs a short patch + validation (approx 2–3 hours).

Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: autoscaler_metrics_0619.csv

Tom — thanks for the trace and for calling this out. I'm available for a quick triage call now and have scheduled a 30-minute bridge at 10:00 PDT. Join link: https://meet.redwood.ai/velox-triage-0619.

Agenda for the call:
- Readout of our telemetry and the three proposed mitigations (Marcus)
- Walk through Velox trace and mapping to our request logs (Tom + Velox ops)
- Short-term action that Velox and Redwood can take (timeout/retry tuning, model-variant routing)

Thanks — Monica

Cc: Blake Thompson <blake_thompson@redwood.ai>, Leadership <leadership@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive brief: Velox impact & recommended remediation

Team / Leadership — brief summary and ask:

What happened:
- On 2027-06-19 20:28 PDT, Velox's dedicated pool hit the concurrency ceiling causing the router to shed requests (429s) and a p99 latency increase for a ~45-minute window. The root chain includes: concurrency cap hit -> KV-cache warmup CPU bursts on subset of hosts -> scheduler delays -> autoscaler slow due to region quota, leading to sustained degradation.

Customer impact:
- Checkout throughput for several Velox enterprise accounts degraded by ~30% during the window; Velox flagged revenue-impacting checkout errors and engaged ops. They requested an incident explanation and potential SLA remediation.

Actions taken / in-flight:
- Increased concurrency cap for the dedicated pool from 120 -> 180 as an emergency mitigation (rolled at 11:00 PDT).
- Enabled model-variant fallback for low-priority routes (quantized variant) to reduce per-token compute.
- Patch to scheduler prioritization queued; targeted canary planned for 13:00 PDT (estimated 2–3 hours to validate).
- Monica scheduled customer triage and is owning post-incident communication and credit proposal.

Recommended exec asks:
1) Approval to offer a one-time SLA credit for impacted billing period (estimated credit: 5–8% of monthly invoice) — approval required from Finance.
2) Short-term operational commitment: allow emergency increase of concurrency caps for this customer's dedicated pool for the next 48 hours to stabilize traffic while we roll the scheduler patch.
3) Approve the scheduler patch canary and fast-path rollout (engineering time + limited risk).

Risk/notes: increasing concurrency cap raises per-host memory pressure and may increase OOM risk on older hosts; Marcus's team will only roll to hosts with headroom. The scheduler patch will reduce head-of-line blocking but must be validated for regressions on throughput.

Please reply with approvals or questions.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
